constructorContract.observation: Abstract types, value types including record structs, interfaces and types with no public constructors return null. Record recognition requires the public instance <Clone>$ method returning the type or its immediate base type. Ordinary C# primary-constructor classes are not admitted merely because they have matching properties.

Exactly one public constructor with at least one parameter is required. Each parameter must have some visible property with an ordinal, case-sensitive equal name and exactly equal reflected Type; assignability and conversion are not used. Extra properties are permitted. Declaration order is not required: the loop only checks existence and returns the sole constructor, not the matched properties.

The producer is GetVisibleProperties, not raw Type.GetProperties. Interesting properties have public instance non-indexed getters and are not byref-like. A setter is not required. Inherited properties hidden by a closer same-name declaration are removed; the closer-declaration lookup includes public/non-public, static/instance declarations. Replacing this with raw reflection or a name-only type lookup could admit a hidden or wrong-type member.

producerAndReuse.observation: Default MVC registration makes the metadata provider a singleton and includes the default binding-details provider in the metadata-details pipeline.

Model metadata is cached by ModelMetadataIdentity; BindingMetadata and constructor metadata are lazy retained details. The target scan is not repeated for each ordinary request using the same initialized metadata. Distinct identities/providers and unsynchronized concurrent first use can still repeat it; there is no globally once-per-Type guarantee.

The real binder producer consumes the selected constructor metadata to create parameter binders. The metadata provider builds constructor parameter metadata and a compiled invoker; object creation uses that invoker. Request collection cardinality does not change a record type's reflected constructor cardinality.

MVC's metadata-update service clears the metadata-provider cache and signals action-descriptor changes. PropertyHelper has its own metadata-update handler clearing both property caches. No new retained state or cache was introduced, so no additional hot-reload mechanism is proposed. This was traced in source, not validated through a live metadata delta.

materiality.scanShape: At most parameters times visible properties, with early exit on an unmatched parameter. No timing, allocation or performance counters were gathered.
materiality.nativeFixtureRange: 52 existing record declarations, one through four constructor parameters. Address13 at line 2733 has four parameters; Person6 and Person7 have three.
materiality.limits: The fixture inventory is not an exhaustive application inventory or proof that wider customer records do not exist. Rebuilding metadata in a synthetic loop or inventing giant records would not establish a material ordinary-MVC workload.
materiality.decision: No surgical optimization is justified by the evidence collected. Retain the finding as an understood source shape, not a performance-qualified or publishable change.
